text:
Ana: Opening a quick thread: weneed a model for per-tenant TLS proxying for Private endpoints. Problem: customers want control over certs + TLS context for compliance (client certs, CAA enforcement) but we also want to avoid full VPC peering. Options: 1) terminate TLS at our regional proxy with per-tenant certs we manage, 2) passthrough TLS and let customer's agent terminate, 3) SNI routing to a tenant-side relay container. Tradeoffs?
Jon: Option 1 is simplest operationally for us (we can inspect headers, inject tokens, and do routing). But customers with strict key custody won't allow our CA to sign their leaf certs. Also breaks end-to-end mTLS expectations.
Priya: Option 2 keeps E2E but means we cannot reliably apply L7 controls (authz, header enrichment). And routing by SNI alone is brittle for non-hostname TLS (IP-based services) or when clients use TLS session resumption across different frontends.
Marco: Could we do a hybrid: accept TLS on proxy but support "customer-provided certs" via an automated CSR flow. Customer uploads CSR or we integrate with their ACME/KMS to sign ephemeral certs that we only store in memory on edge nodes. That might satisfy custody concerns if they sign locally and send cert+chain.
Ana: Let's enumerate requirements: - must support customer-managed keys (optional), - minimal latency delta (<5ms median), - support for mtls client certs when the customer requires it, - allow L7 features for opt-in customers, - work in air-gapped private installs.
Jon: For air-gapped/private installs the obvious approach is to run the TLS ingress inside customer network (a small relay) and then connect upstream over an authenticated tunnel to our control plane. That keeps keys local. But adds operational burden + HA concerns.
Priya: Idea: introduce a "TLS termination shim" running as part of the agent in-customer VPC. The shim accepts inbound SNI connections and does termination, then forwards decrypted traffic over a mutually authenticated tunnel to our regional relay. We keep headers and L7 hooks only for the tunneled flow. That avoids peering and keeps keys local.
Marco: That matches how some CDNs do origin pull. Questions: how do we handle client mTLS? The shim must validate client certs against customer CA. Then the shim should send a canonicalized client identity to our relay (e.g., X-Client-CN) over the mTLS control tunnel, signed with ephemeral session keys to prevent spoofing.
Ana: Good point. We need cryptographic binding so relays can't impersonate client certs. Propose: shim signs a short assertion: {client_cn, nonce, timestamp, upstream_session_id} signed with the agent's key. Relay verifies agent sig using agent cert provisioned by controlplane.
Jon: Operational note: we must rotate agent certs and support key revocation quickly. Agent bootstrap can use customer's OIDC/KMS to fetch certs; agent certs should be short lived (hours) to reduce blast radius.
Priya: Another dimension: how do we do certificate issuance for hosted customers who want "their" hostname? Options: delegate ACME to customer (they provision certs to us), or we offer a managed cert service where we obtain certs on their behalf but provide audit logs + optional upload of private key to customer KMS (less ideal).
Marco: Mechanism: support two flows: a) customer-key-first: customer supplies cert+privkey via KMS-integrated upload (for Private); b) CSR-flow: agent generates keypair, sends CSR to customer's CA endpoint or to our CA if customer allows. We should record which flow used in the tenant config.
Ana: Performance: terminating TLS in shim vs at our regional relay matters. In-path shim introduces extra hop but we can use high-performance TLS libs (BoringSSL with TLS 1.3 session resumption) and keep the tunnel multiplexed to reduce latency. For most requests, additional hop should be <10ms inter-region if placed in same region. We'll measure.
Jon: Edge case: clients using IP allowlists that expect stable remote IPs. If TLS shim lives in customer's VPC, egress IPs are customer's; if shim is in our relay, they see our egress IP. We must surface this in product docs.
Priya: Security: attack surface for forged X-Client headers. MUST always verify agent sig and reject any identity assertions not verifiable. Add telemetry: client_identity_assertions_verified, assertion_replay_attempts.
Marco: For routing, SNI fallback needed when hostname absent. We can add ALPN-based routing or use SNI + destination IP mapping learned from controlplane registration. Also, support TLS-over-TCP for non-HTTP protocols by tunneling raw bytes.
Ana: Implementation plan sketch: - Phase 1: PoC shim that terminates TLS, validates client cert, signs assertion, tunnels to regional relay. No managed cert issuance yet. - Phase 2: add CSR and CSR-proxy flow, UI in console to register cert source, add metrics. - Phase 3: GA with opt-in, add KMS integrate for hosted customers.
Jon: Monitoring: per-tenant metrics: tls_sessions, tls_handshake_ms_p50/p95, client_cert_validations, assertion_failures, agent_cert_revocations. Set alert if assertion_failures > 0.1% for 1h.
Priya: Threat model notes: shim compromise could leak private keys. Recommend HSM integration on appliances for high-security customers or restrict shim to run on a dedicated subnet with minimal access. Also provide a revocation API that can forcibly disable agent assertions immediately.
Marco: Ownering: I'll take Phase 1 proxy perf bench. Priya take threat model + revocation API. Jon take cert issuance UX and migrations. Ana will coordinate with product/legal for KMS requirements.
infra-bot: created task E2E-TLS-SHIM-POC: https://internal/tasks/E2E-TLS-SHIM-1 (owners: Marco,Priya,Jon)
Ana: Let's demo the PoC in next arch sync. I'll create #tls-shim-poc channel and add folks. TL;DR: shim lets customers keep keys local while enabling L7 features over an authenticated tunnel; roll out opt-in for Private/Dedicated first. :white_check_mark:
